title: Graphs and Shifts
subtitle: The basic graphs by sight, and what shifting, flipping and stretching do to them.

questions.text: Match each description to its function.
pairs: starts at the origin, rises, then flattens
two separate branches that never touch the axes
an S shape through the origin
questions.explain: These five, plus straight lines, are the starting point for most graphs in this course.

questions.text: $y = f(x) - 5$ moves the graph of $f$
questions.explain: Outside the function: it changes the outputs, so it is vertical, and it does what it says.

questions.text: $y = f(x + 1)$ moves the graph of $f$
questions.explain: Inside the function: sideways, and backwards from what the sign suggests.
Every height becomes its opposite, so the picture turns upside down.

options: makes the graph twice as wide
questions.explain: Each output is multiplied by 2. Points on the $x$-axis stay put.

questions.text: The lowest point of $y = (x - 3)^2 + 2$ is at $(3, 2)$.
questions.explain: $y = x^2$ has its lowest point at $(0, 0)$. Right 3 and up 2 moves it to $(3, 2)$.

slides.text: A handful of graphs come up all year. You should know each one on sight. Which function is this?
slides.hint: It starts at the origin and only exists for $x >= 0$.
slides.explain: $sqrt(x)$: it starts at $(0, 0)$, rises quickly, then flattens out.

slides.text: The dashed curve is $f(x) = x^2$ moved **up 3**. Move your graph onto it, and watch the formula change as you go.
slides.hint: Tap ↑ until your curve sits on the dashed one.
slides.explain: Adding 3 **outside** the function raises every output by 3: $y = f(x) + 3$.

slides.text: Now the dashed curve is $f(x) = x^2$ moved **right 2**. Move yours, and look closely at the sign in the formula.
slides.explain: Right 2 is $f(x - 2)$, with a **minus**. A change inside the parentheses acts on $x$, and it acts backwards.

slides.text: So the graph of $y = (x + 4)^2$ is the graph of $y = x^2$ moved
slides.hint: It is inside the parentheses, so it is sideways, and backwards.
slides.explain: $(x + 4)^2$ is zero when $x = -4$, so the bottom of the parabola moved to $x = -4$: left 4.

slides.text: A minus sign in front flips the graph over the $x$-axis. This target has been flipped **and** moved. Match it.
slides.hint: Flip first. Then find where the top of the dashed curve is.

slides.text: Now read it straight from a formula. $y = -sqrt(x - 3) + 1$ is the graph of $y = sqrt(x)$
slides.hint: Inside the root: sideways and backwards. Outside: up and down. In front: flip.
slides.explain: $-$ in front: flipped. $x - 3$ inside: right 3. $+ 1$ outside: up 1.
